people.name: Begüm Aydin, Ph.D.
people.bio:
Begüm is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Genetics and Development at Columbia University Irving Medical Center and a member of the Columbia Stem Cell Initiative. She earned her B.Sc. in Molecular Biology and Genetics from Boğaziçi University in Istanbul before moving to New York City for her Ph.D. in Biology at New York University. During her doctoral work with Esteban Mazzoni, Begüm studied the intrinsic developmental programs that control neuronal differentiation using embryonic stem cell models. As a postdoctoral fellow at The Rockefeller University with Daniel Mucida, she expanded this work to ask how the environment shapes nervous system development and maintenance, focusing on interactions between the gut microbiota and the enteric nervous system. Her research identified microbial species and signals that promote neuronal recovery, revealing environmentally driven plasticity in the enteric nervous system and its broader relevance to neuronal regeneration.

Begüm was a Junior Fellow of the Simons Society of Fellows and is an HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellow, supporting her transition to an independent, interdisciplinary research program at Columbia. .
